description: Route-level bundle size budgets for authenticated Next.js pages. Budgets cover the First Load JS (shared chunks + page chunk) for each route segment. Values are in bytes. Measured values are filled by the post-build bundle analyzer and compared against the declared ceiling by the orchestrator. A null measured value means the route has not been profiled yet.

network.mobile: ~1.6 Mbps down, 750 Kbps up, 150ms RTT — close to Fast 3G+ (frontend/scripts/measure-web-vitals.mjs MOBILE_PROFILE: 1,600,000/8 bytes/s down, 750,000/8 bytes/s up, 150ms latency)

cpu.mobile: 4x CPU slowdown (Chrome DevTools mid-tier mobile preset)

referenceProfile.notes: Measured by frontend/scripts/measure-web-vitals.mjs, which drives a headless Chrome over the DevTools Protocol against `next build && next start`; the earlier claim that these came from Lighthouse 12 in CI was not true of anything in this repository. Field data (CrUX) is the source of truth for production; lab data here is the gating proxy. The 100ms responsiveness rule (CLAUDE.md section 12.2) is enforced by INP <= 200ms and measured directly as perceivedResponsiveness in the capture. measuredFirstLoadJsBytes is gzip(9) summed over the unique chunks in each route's page_client-reference-manifest.js from a production build, and measuredPageChunkBytes is the additive over the /dashboard baseline — both produced by scripts/measure-route-bundles.mjs. measuredScriptBytes, measuredCssBytes, measuredImageBytes, measuredFontBytes, measuredThirdPartyBytes, measuredServerPayloadBytes and measuredTotalBytes are over-the-wire encoded bytes from a cold-cache navigation, produced by measure-web-vitals.mjs. measuredScriptBytes is roughly twice measuredFirstLoadJsBytes on this app because hydration fetches chunks the client-reference manifest does not list.

/mail.note: Mail shell — first-load budget is higher because DOMPurify (isomorphic-dompurify) is a non-trivial dependency; compose sheet, AI toolbar and inbox summary sheet are lazy-loaded via next/dynamic. PASSES: 507kB < 614kB ceiling
/mail.imageBudgetNote: The shell paints one brand mark (public/logo.svg, 2,872 B over the wire) and a cold-cache load requests it twice, once for the loading screen and once for the header. The previous declaration of 0 asserted the route ships no image at all, which measurement contradicts; 8 kB is the honest ceiling for one brand mark and it still fails if a route starts shipping photography.
/mail.breachOwnerNote: Over-the-wire JS breach is shared-shell weight, not this route's own composition. The /dashboard baseline is 39 chunks / 440,065 B gzip by the client-reference-manifest method and 640,260 B actually downloaded; the largest identifiable library in it is framer-motion at 224 kB raw / 71 kB gzip, imported by 278 files across app/, components/ and features/ and required by the frozen public landing animations, so it is an architecture decision rather than a lazy boundary. Measured on build 5KxS0uW9Wrm0BIVYZicTs, 2026-09-02. CORRECTION to ticket 27's P1 relay: ably is NOT in the first load of /dashboard, /mail or /inbox at this commit — it appears only in /chat (208 kB raw / 58 kB gzip), where it is that route's own realtime client.

budgetExceptions.reason: Authenticated TTFB is a backend round trip, not a page cost. GET /auth/session-data/:userId measures 588-756 ms against the Neon instance in ap-southeast-1, and lib/auth-session.ts issues it twice on a non-2xx. The same production server returns the public landing page in 5-18 ms TTFB, so no part of this number is bundle, route composition or render.
Same cause as the mobile TTFB exception; the desktop profile applies no network emulation, so its TTFB is the server render alone and still breaches 400 ms by a factor of three.
FCP cannot precede TTFB. With TTFB at 1.4-2.5 s of server time the 1,800 ms FCP budget is already spent before the first byte; it is not separately actionable until the TTFB exception is closed.
Same dependency as the mobile FCP exception.
LCP cannot precede FCP, which cannot precede TTFB.

INP was NOT measured in the 2026-09-02 capture and this entry claims nothing about it. The driver's interaction probe found no eligible control because the shell never rendered one: /me/access is refused on this machine, so the app paints its access-failure state instead of the product. An unmeasured budget is not a met budget and check-web-vitals-budget still reports it as not measured.

budgetExceptionsNote: An exception records who owns a breach and why. It is annotation only: check-web-vitals-budget.mjs prints it next to the failure and still exits non-zero, and its self-test asserts that an exception never reduces the failure count. Nothing here makes a red budget green.
